page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 32 GB of system memory (4 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The defining feature of this instance is the dedicated accelerator: one NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. It includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached block storage for operating systems and persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate that host CPU performance is comparatively modest. In compute testing, the instance produced a single-core Geekbench score of 604.0 and a multi-core score of 2324.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 6136.75 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 5895.65, placing host-level processing in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth remains mixed, recording 39.02 GB/sec on large read blocks and 35.65 GB/sec on large write blocks. These numbers emphasize that the host architecture serves primarily to feed data into the GPU subsystem rather than conduct intensive CPU-bound calculations.

Because the primary compute density resides within the NVIDIA V100 accelerator, ecs.gn6v-c8g1.2xlarge functions best for GPU-accelerated computing, deep learning inference, model fine-tuning within the 16 GB VRAM ceiling, and scientific simulations. Deployments requiring intense CPU preprocessing, heavy data compression, or fast local scratch disks will face architectural bottlenecks due to the lower-tier CPU scores, 2 Gbps baseline network capacity, and absence of local disks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server designed for compute workloads that offload processing to dedicated hardware. Built on an Intel Xeon 8163 CPU running at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores), 32 GB of RAM, and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU with 16 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. Benchmark indicators reveal modest host-level CPU performance, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2324.0 and PassMark CPU score of 6136.75, showing that system throughput is tightly tethered to the GPU rather than the host processor. The instance contains no integrated local storage, requiring network storage for data persistence. This profile is engineered specifically for deep learning inference, mid-tier model training, computer vision tasks, and GPU-driven scientific computations where GPU acceleration offsets modest host processor speeds.
